user_goal.text: Report the titles of the tasks due on the asked date in Tasks app, returning titles only and using a comma-separated list if there are multiple.

benchmark_success.text: Native success requires the run to finish with `done=true`, and the submitted answer text to pass `check_agent_answer` for this task: after splitting on commas and trimming whitespace, the answer must have the same item count as the expected due-date titles, and each returned item must fuzzy-match at least one expected title under the evaluator's STRING_MATCH rule.

checked_by.text: AndroidWorld runner completion gate plus `InformationRetrieval.is_successful`, which delegates answer checking to `proto_utils.check_agent_answer` for the initialized Tasks-app state.

decisive_artifacts.artifact: Episode trace or action log with termination status and submitted answer text
decisive_artifacts.question: Does retained run evidence show `done=true` or `done=false`, and what exact answer text, if any, was submitted to the environment?

decisive_artifacts.artifact: Initialized Tasks-app state snapshot for this run
decisive_artifacts.question: Which task titles were initialized with `due_date` equal to this task's target date?

success_if.text: Retained evidence shows the episode finished with `done=true`, and the submitted answer, after comma splitting and trimming, has the same number of items as the initialized target-date titles and every returned item fuzzy-matches at least one of those titles under the evaluator's case-insensitive STRING_MATCH rule.

fail_if.text: Retained evidence shows the episode ended with `done=false`.
A complete retained trace shows the run finished but no answer text was submitted before termination, so `interaction_cache` remained empty.

Retained evidence shows `done=true`, but the submitted answer fails the native comparator: the comma-split item count differs from the expected target-date title count, or at least one returned item fails to fuzzy-match any expected title.

undecided_if.text: Retained evidence does not preserve enough run-execution detail to determine whether the episode finished with `done=true` and what answer text, if any, was submitted.
Retained evidence does not preserve the initialized Tasks-app target-date titles, so the evaluator's expected answers cannot be reconstructed from stored underlying state.

additional_conditions.text: Beyond native scoring, the answer lists every task title due on the target date exactly once, using the exact title text from the initialized Tasks-app state rather than a merely fuzzy near-match or repeated title.
additional_conditions.rationale: The official prompt asks for the tasks due on the date as titles only, but native scoring only checks equal answer length and whether each returned item fuzzy-matches at least one expected title under a 0.9 similarity threshold; it does not require exact text or complete one-to-one coverage of all expected titles.

decisive_artifacts.question: What exact comma-separated answer text was submitted?
